advisories.summary: mergeObject() accepts attacker-controlled keys that can poison the returned object's prototype.
advisories.runtime_disposition_evidence: Pinned Education 93bc7075753369457919720690f80c6d2207b5f2 frontend/yarn.lock and HRMS a4768b441cff346def505e27f2a2229ee1e05b9b frontend/yarn.lock resolve deepmerge 4.3.1 transitively. In the editor chain, @tiptap/pm 2.2.3 -> prosemirror-trailing-node -> @remirror/core-helpers (3.0.0 Education; 2.0.3 HRMS): the pinned trailing-node implementation imports includes and uniqueArray, not deepMerge, and the reviewed production Vite bundle did not include deepmerge. HRMS also resolves deepmerge through @rollup/plugin-node-resolve 15.3.1 under workbox-build 7.3.0; this invocation is build-time deepMerge({}, defaults) with internally constructed objects, not attacker-controlled source objects. No reachable use of vulnerable mergeObject() with untrusted source keys was established on the inspected pinned dependency paths. See README.md; future dependency/call-path changes require new review.
advisories.fix_path: No patched deepmerge version is published in the GitHub-reviewed advisory as of this assessment. Reassess on pinned Education/HRMS dependency updates or a newly reachable attacker-controlled deepMerge call; do not blanket-approve other deepmerge consumers.
